All four read SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors against a stand-in Decimal; a probe gives correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day in all four), top customers with zero-count customers left out, empty results for [], and {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status and a bad date. Sonnet-2's final reply is prose ending in '/pr' rather than just the file path; no rule in the list covers that.

git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ equals git diff HEAD -- idiomatic-elixir/: one new SKILL.md rule, "Keep a `->` clause on one line only when its pattern and body are each one plain term", and nothing else. The other ten listed rules are unchanged and graded to the standard of 2026-10-23/grades/order-report-skill.json (Enum.count or length/1 of a filtered list that also feeds the totals held clean; prepend without reverse held clean when nothing downstream depends on order; string_field/2 held clean under Naming). All ten are clean in all four runs, as in the previous sweep.

New rule, graded against its current text and the case file's new bullet. Exercised in 4 of 4 runs (every run has case clauses; sonnet-2 also a with ... else clause). Violated in 2 of 4: haiku-2 and sonnet-1, both by the same clause in string_field/2, decided by "A pattern that holds a binary, a guard or nesting ... goes on the line after the `->`.": haiku-2 line 72 and sonnet-1 line 128, "{:ok, value} when is_binary(value) -> {:ok, value}". Haiku-1 and sonnet-2 are clean. Sonnet-2 is also the only run that exercises "Once one clause breaks, `mix format` moves every clause's body down and separates the clauses with a blank line; keep that layout": build/1's case at lines 86-91 has both clauses broken with a blank line between, held clean.

Reading used for bodies, which decides the two clean runs: a body is held clean unless it holds what the second sentence names, "a nested call or a string built with `#{}`"; a tuple wrapping one call with plain arguments, such as haiku-1 line 30 "{:ok, orders} -> {:ok, report(orders)}" and sonnet-2 line 186 "{:ok, datetime, _utc_offset} -> {:ok, DateTime.to_date(datetime)}", is not counted as a nested call, and nested tuple literals such as "{:ok, order} -> {:cont, {:ok, [order | orders]}}" count as one literal. The skill itself supports this reading: the with rule's own 'write' example keeps "{:ok, orders} -> {:ok, summarize(orders)}" on one line. Under the stricter reading of the first sentence ("the body is one call or one literal", so a tuple holding a call is neither), all four runs would be violated: haiku-1 line 30, haiku-2 lines 35 and 44, sonnet-1 lines 81, 91 and 158, sonnet-2 line 186. The rule text and the with rule's example disagree on this shape; one of them should be changed so the next sweep can grade it without a reading. Patterns of the form "{:error, _reason} = error" are held to be one plain term (a one-level tuple with an alias), not nesting. Haiku-2 line 44, "nil -> {:ok, Enum.map(parsed, fn {:ok, order} -> order end)}", holds an fn inside a call inside a tuple; it is not used to decide haiku-2, which line 72 already decides.

Other rules: haiku-1's @doc on build/1 has no ## Examples (listed under other_violations); the other three have doctest examples. Sonnet-2's multi-line parse_order/1 head binds the five required keys with a catch-all below, so the keys select by presence and the head-binding rule is held clean as in the previous sweep; its = row alias is not a bound field. Sonnet-1 pipes into case at line 90 (|> case do), which no rule forbids. No other violation was found.
